reasons: Link reading is covered by tests.
Viewer settings have no tests in the packet.
Storage failures are ignored silently by design.

terms.meaning: browser storage kept only for one tab until that tab closes

sections.name: SavedRoute
sections.title: Saved route shape
sections.what: Defines a saved link as a job id plus an optional project id.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared shape for the reading and writing code.

sections.name: parseSavedRoute
sections.title: Reading a saved link
sections.what: Reads an address hash, accepts only the programme or project model forms, decodes the project name, and refuses names with slashes or control characters.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops crafted addresses from pointing at unexpected paths.
sections.watch_out: Job ids accept only letters, digits and dashes, so ids with other characters will not open.

sections.name: savedRoute
sections.title: Writing a saved link
sections.what: Builds an address hash from a job id and optional project id, encoding both so special characters stay safe.
sections.why: Likely reason: the matching writer for the reading function.
sections.watch_out: The written form must match the read pattern, so a change to one needs a matching change to the other.

sections.name: readViewerState
sections.title: Reading viewer settings
sections.what: Loads saved viewer settings from session storage as an object. Returns an empty object if nothing is stored or the data is not an object.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives a safe default when storage is empty or the data is damaged.
sections.watch_out: Damaged stored data is replaced by defaults with no warning.

sections.name: writeViewerState
sections.title: Saving viewer settings
sections.what: Saves viewer settings to session storage as JSON and ignores any failure.
sections.why: Likely reason: some browsers block storage, and the app should keep working when they do.
sections.watch_out: A failed save gives no message, so a user may lose settings without knowing it.

summary: Builds and reads the in-app address that names a job and optionally a project. It also saves small viewer settings in the browser's session storage.
purpose: Lets a visitor reopen the same job or project from its address.
why: Likely reason: the app keeps its view in the address hash, and session storage keeps viewer settings for the current tab.
how: The read function matches the address shape, decodes the project name, refuses names with slashes or control characters, and returns both ids. The write function encodes both values into the address. Viewer settings are read and written as JSON, and storage failures are ignored.
inputs: An address hash string, a job id and optional project id, and a storage key with a value.
outputs: An object with job and project ids, or nothing for a bad address. A link string. Stored settings, or an empty object when none exist.
risks: Job ids may contain only letters, digits and dashes, so other characters make a link unreadable. Storage failures are ignored silently, so settings can be lost without any message.
debug: If a link does not open, check the job id against the allowed characters. If settings do not persist, check whether the browser blocks session storage.
